metadata.indication: Treatment of recurrent malignant glioblastoma multiforme.

catalogue_reconciliation.scope_note: The NCCP states that its website list is not comprehensive. This reconciliation does not assert that every possible national regimen is published online.

encoding_maturity.label: Source reconciled; independent clinical/pharmacy review pending
encoding_maturity.scope_note: Fresh NCCP 00813 v2 and EMA reviewed. Timing, persistent toxicity and previous discontinuation are assessed separately. No numeric adverse-event dose reductions are inferred. Independent clinical/pharmacy approval remains pending.

clinical_governance.prescriptive_authority: The treatment plan must be initiated by a Consultant Medical Oncologist.
clinical_governance.dose_modification_note: Bevacizumab dose reduction for adverse events is not recommended. Temporarily withhold or discontinue according to the source-specific event, history and recovery; no numerical toxicity dose ladder.
clinical_governance.disclaimer: Decision-support encoding derived from NCCP 00813 Version 2. It does not replace the current official regimen, prescribing review, pharmacy verification or independent clinical judgement.

indications.description: Treatment of recurrent malignant glioblastoma multiforme.

treatment.schedule_summary: Bevacizumab 5 mg/kg IV on Day 1 every 14 days until progression or unacceptable toxicity.
treatment.duration_text: Continue every 14 days until progression or unacceptable toxicity.

components.note: Dilute in 100 mL sodium chloride 0.9%. First infusion over 90 minutes; second over 60 minutes only if the first is tolerated; subsequent infusions over 30 minutes only if 60 minutes is tolerated. Flush with sodium chloride before and after; do not mix with glucose or give IV push/bolus. Rapid infusion requires a separate off-label consent and local governance process.

uncertainties: NCCP initiation blood pressure >150/100 does not specify AND/OR between components. Numerical readings trigger review; clinician-confirmed uncontrolled status is assessed separately.
NCCP uses recent intracranial haemorrhage without a numerical interval; no number of days is inferred.
Grade 2–3 hypertension prompts antihypertensive therapy and consideration of interruption. Persisting grade 3 requires explicit clinical confirmation.
Source event grading is not automatically converted from NCI-CTCAE v3 to CTCAE v5.
Previous proteinuria >4 g/24 h or another source-directed discontinuation is not erased by a subsequent normal result.
NCCP expects no renal/hepatic dose adjustment, while EMA notes these populations have not been studied. Eligibility, monitoring and toxicity assessment remain required.
Concurrent discordant dipstick and quantitative results require confirmation of timing and collection validity; a current 4+ screening result is not silently overridden.
